title: Mass automated login attempts hit Germany's BundID citizen accounts; password login suspended, later restored with two-factor authentication
date_note: Date of the first reports (dpa, 16 November); Tichys Einblick says the attack hit on Monday, which is 16 November.
summary: Unknown attackers ran automated mass login attempts against BundID, Germany's federal citizen account. Per dpa and Handelsblatt, citing the BSI, protections triggered, affected accounts were blocked and password login was temporarily disabled; eID and Elster logins still worked. Tichys Einblick reported on 18 November that the ministry later said there was no explicit blocking, and that password login returned with two-factor authentication. Officials say they have no evidence of data theft.
plain: Attackers tried mass logins to German citizen accounts used for government services. Password login was paused and later returned with a second login step; officials say they have no evidence of data theft.
exec: A national government login service was targeted at scale; password login was suspended, which may have disrupted access to public services.
action: As the BundID portal advised, per dpa, use the online ID card (eID) or an Elster certificate to sign in; Tichys Einblick reports password login now requires two-factor authentication.

sources.name: Volksstimme (dpa): Angriffe auf BundID: Zugriffsmöglichkeiten eingeschränkt
